 Live Updates Updated Mon, Oct 26 2026 9:40 AM EDT Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Anthropic IPO live updates: AI lab lost $80.7 billion in first half of 2026
 Ashley Capoot Annie Palmer This is CNBC's live coverage of Anthropic's historic IPO filing. 
 watch now VIDEO 8:18 08:18 Anthropic files SEC prospectus, bringing AI lab a step closer to historic offering Squawk on the Street Anthropic is officially headed for the public market in what is expected to be a historic offering for a five-year-old company that's been at the heart of the generative artificial intelligence boom. 
 In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission , Anthropic said it plans to list on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol "ANT."
 The company behind Claude confidentially filed with the SEC in June, giving the agency time to review its financials before they were made available to the public and prospective investors. 
 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the company in 2021 after he and a small group of researchers defected from OpenAI , now its chief rival. Anthropic's Claude model and services have captivated the corporate world, as companies have opened their wallets in an effort to crack new growth opportunities and find internal efficiencies. 
 Expansion has accelerated in 2026, driven largely by the popularity of AI coding tool Claude Code , and powerful models including Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 . The company has been racing to maintain an edge over competitors like OpenAI and Google , and faced sharp criticism over its positions on safety, regulation and national security, leading to two high-profile disputes with the U.S. government in recent months.
 Anthropic's offering, if it doesn't get derailed, will land just a few months after Elon Musk's SpaceX debuted on the Nasdaq in by far the biggest IPO on record, ultimately raising $85.7 billion. It's been a volatile stretch for SpaceX shares, which finished last week slightly below where they opened in June.
 As it prepares to hit the market, Anthropic has to contend with severe jitters on Wall Street as concerns grow over whether spending on AI services will justify the trillions of dollars in expected infrastructure costs. So-called neoclouds like CoreWeave and Nebius have been hammered of late, losing over 30% of their value in October as credit risk is rising across the data center space. 
 What you need to know about the IPO: 
 Here's what Anthropic's top execs get paid 
 Billions in commitments with Microsoft 
 Anthropic reports $80.7 billion loss in first half of 2026
 Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the lead underwriters 
 CNBC's reporters are covering Anthropic's IPO from bureaus in San Francisco and Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey. 
 3 Min Ago Anthropic agreed to pay SpaceX $3.1 billion per month for compute
 Anthropic will pay SpaceX around $3.1 billion per month to "access compute powered by NVIDIA GPUs," once all promised capacity is delivered, the filing said. The company has agreed to spend up to $120.5 billion over a period extending into 2029.
 Anthropic's filing said the company has other agreements with Microsoft , Nscale, Lambda and other cloud providers to provide "compute capacity powered by Nvidia GPUS." 
 —Lora Kolodny 
 4 Min Ago Anthropic could use net proceeds to 'acquire or invest in businesses, products, services, or technologies' 
 Anthropic said it intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for "general corporate purposes," including capital expenditures, working capital, operating expenses and hiring and retention of "highly skilled personnel."
 The company said it may also use a portion of the net proceeds to "acquire or invest in businesses, products, services, or technologies." 
 "However, we do not have agreements or commitments for any material acquisitions or investments at this time," the filing says. 
 —Ashley Capoot 
 5 Min Ago How much Anthropic's top brass gets paid
 According to Monday's filing, Amodei's compensation totaled $17.96 million in 2025, with the vast majority coming from stock and options awards. His base salary was $654,167. 
 His sister, Daniela Amodei, was the second-highest paid executive at $16.4 million for 2025. Her base salary is the same as her brother's. 
 Both Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei received raises in 2025 and two pay bumps this year. Both executives' base salary was increased to $1.38 million, effective July 1, according to the release. 
 Anthropic CFO Krisha Rao earned a base salary of $706,250 in 2025, and following several salary increases, his base salary now reaches $1.25 million, effective July 1. 
 — Annie Palmer 
 6 Min Ago Anthropic has nearly $45 billion in commitments with Microsoft, which is also a rival
 Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella speaks at a Microsoft Frontier Tour event in the CNIT building at La Defense business district in Puteaux, near Paris, on October 20, 2026. Dimitar Dilkoff | Afp | Getty Images Microsoft announced plans to invest $5 billion in Anthropic last November in a funding round valuing the lab in the range of $350 billion . In May, Anthropic said it had raised funds at a $965 billion valuation, and weeks later, Microsoft disclosed a $3.2 billion gain on its stake.
 At the time of its investment announcement last year, Microsoft said Anthropic would bring its Claude large language models to the Microsoft Azure cloud, widening access to software developers. Plus, Anthropic signed on to spend $30 billion on Azure and contracting as much as a gigawatt worth of additional computing power.
 Anthropic and Microsoft have modified the November 2025 agreement such that Anthropic now intends to spend with Microsoft at least $44.9 billion between November 2026 and May 2023. The deal can't be canceled unless Microsoft has an uncured material breach or an undelivered tranche.
 Anthropic said in Monday's prospectus that it pays fees to Microsoft — plus Amazon and Google — in a joint go-to-market arrangement to gain a direct relationship with customers.
 Plus, Anthropic counts on Microsoft, as well as Amazon, Google and Broadcom, for computing power in relationships that "create dependencies and potential vulnerabilities." 
 Microsoft has integrated Claude models into the GitHub Copilot coding tool, the Foundry model garden and Copilot Cowork , a product that takes on complex productivity tasks. At the same time, Microsoft has been advertising the capabilities of models it has built in house , at times touting advantages over Anthropic alternatives.
 "Amazon, Google, and Microsoft each offer AI services and develop and deploy competing AI models through their respective cloud platforms," Anthropic said.
 Additionally, Christopher Liddell, a former Microsoft finance chief, joined Anthropic's board in February, according to the filing.
 "To the extent these CSPs promote, integrate, prioritize, or provide customer access to our models, platform, and applications on terms that are less favorable than those applicable to their own competing offerings or to the offerings of other companies, including with respect to pricing, commercial terms, product placement, integration, or access to compute or sales incentives, our competitive position, customer adoption, and business results could be adversely affected," Anthropic said.
 — Jordan Novet 
 13 Min Ago Anthropic says its capital and governance structure has 'no direct public company precedent'
 Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, during the World Economic Forum (WEF) in Davos, Switzerland, on Tuesday, Jan. 20, 2026. Krisztian Bocsi | Bloomberg | Getty Images Anthropic said it has a novel capital and corporate governance structure that "has no direct public company precedent." 
 "Our governance structure is likely to have the effect of limiting the likelihood of an unsolicited merger proposal, unsolicited tender offer, or proxy contest for the removal of directors," the filing said. "As a result, our governance structure may make it more difficult to replace our directors and management and may have the effect of depriving our stockholders of an opportunity to sell their shares at a premium over prevailing market prices."
 —Ashley Capoot 
 19 Min Ago MIT professor Sinan Aral says enterprise is key to Anthropic's success in the market
 watch now VIDEO 5:51 05:51 MIT's Sinan Aral on Anthropic IPO: Enterprise is key to its market success Squawk Box Sinan Aral, MIT Sloan Professor and AI investor, said on CNBC's "Squawk Box" that Anthropic's ability to be profitable in the enterprise space will determine whether it's an attractive prospect for investors.
 "If you think about the $1.5 to $2 trillion valuation, that's approximately from the low to high end a 22 times to 30 times revenue multiple. So the future growth and the profit of this company are being priced in that kind of valuation," Aral said.
 "The question is, where is the enduring value? And I think the enduring value is going to come from companies that can demonstrate enterprise profitability, productivity, and actual value add, rather than just providing intelligence. I think Anthropic is on the way to doing that ... and I think that is where it will succeed and fail."
 — Caleigh Keating 
 23 Min Ago No single customer represents more than a tenth of Anthropic's revenue
 Anthropic logo and a keyboard in this illustration taken October 19, 2026. Dado Ruvic | Reuters With so many companies relying on Anthropic, the company can say that its business has greater diversification than top artificial intelligence chipmaker Nvidia. 
 "No single customer represented more than 10% of our revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026," Anthropic said in its IPO prospectus.
 Nvidia, by comparison, had five clients that were contributing at least 10% of accounts receivable as of July, according to a filing .
 Anthropic, for its part, reported that five customers accounted for about a quarter of its revenue for the first nine months of 2026.
 "We anticipate that we will continue to derive a significant portion of our revenue from a limited number of customers for the foreseeable future, and in some cases, the portion of our revenue attributable to certain customers may increase in the future," the AI lab said in the prospectus.
 At the end of 2026, revenue from customers that buy through cloud marketplaces represented 48% of revenue, the filing shows.
 — Jordan Novet 
 26 Min Ago Anthropic lost $80.7 billion in the first half of this year
 Anthropic said it lost a staggering $80.7 billion in the first six months of this year, after losing $12.9 billion over the same stretch in 2025. 
 For all of 2025, the company lost about $41.9 billion, widening from a loss of $8.3 billion in 2024. 
 — Annie Palmer 
 27 Min Ago Anthropic reported $16.29 billion in revenue for first half of the year
 Anthropic said revenue increased 1,304% to $16.29 billion in the six months ended June 30, up from $1.16 billion during the same period a year earlier. Revenue for all of last year jumped 1,089% to $4.59 billion.
 —Ashley Capoot 
 32 Min Ago Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are Anthropic's top IPO underwriters
 Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs signage on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York, US, on Friday, April 10, 2026. Michael Nagle | Bloomberg | Getty Images At the top of the prospectus for Anthropic's historic initial public offering, the two biggest investment banks for technology IPOs receive the largest billing. The lead left, as the term is called for the underwriter listed first, is Goldman Sachs. On the right is Morgan Stanley.
 Others banks participating in the share float include JP Morgan, Citigroup, Barclays, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, Deutsche Bank, RBC Capital Markets, UBS Investment Bank, BMO Capital Markets, BNP Paribas, Credit Agricole CIB, Jefferies, Mizuho, MUFG, Societe Generale, TD Securities, BTIG, Cantor, Capital One Securities and Macquarie Capital.
 — Jordan Novet 
 37 Min Ago Who is Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei?
 Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive officer of Anthropic, during a Bloomberg Television interview in San Francisco, California, US, on Tuesday, Dec. 9, 2025. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images Amodei grew up in San Francisco and earned his doctorate degree in biophysics from Princeton University. 
 Prior to starting Anthropic, Amodei, now 43, worked as a senior research scientist at Google Brain, which is now part of AI unit Google DeepMind. Amodei also spent more than four years at OpenAI, where he led the development of models including GPT-2 and GPT-3.
 His sister, Daniela Amodei, is another Anthropic co-founder and serves as the company's president.
 —Ashley Capoot 
 38 Min Ago Anthropic's most recent funding round
 watch now VIDEO 1:35 01:35 Anthropic raises $65B in latest funding round at $965B valuation Power Lunch Anthropic closed its last funding round in May, when it raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation. The financing was led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, and nearly tripled Anthropic's valuation from February, when the company was worth $380 billion. 
 The round was particularly notable because it pushed Anthropic's valuation above OpenAI's for the first time. OpenAI was valued at $852 billion in late March after closing a record-breaking $122 billion funding round. 
 —Ashley Capoot
